examples.question_text:
The table gives monthly repayments in dollars for every $\$1000$ borrowed on a reducing-balance car loan.

| Interest rate p.a. | 24 months | 36 months | 48 months | 60 months |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $8\%$ | 45.23 | 31.34 | 24.41 | 20.28 |
| $9\%$ | 45.68 | 31.80 | 24.89 | 20.76 |
| $10\%$ | 46.14 | 32.27 | 25.36 | 21.25 |

Maya borrows $\$19\,500$ to purchase a car at $10\%$ p.a. over $3$ years. Use the table to calculate her monthly repayment to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
Convert the term to months: $3\times12=36$.

Read the $10\%$ row and the $36$-month column: the repayment is $\$32.27$ per $\$1000$ borrowed.

$\begin{align*}\text{Monthly repayment}&=32.27\times\frac{19\,500}{1000}\\&=32.27\times19.5\\&=\$629.265\\&\approx\$629.27\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
Noah borrows $\$28\,350$ to purchase a car at $9\%$ p.a. over $5$ years. The repayment table gives $\$20.76$ per month for every $\$1000$ borrowed at this rate and term.

Calculate:
a. the monthly repayment to the nearest cent
b. the total amount repaid
c. the total interest paid.

Use the rounded monthly repayment when calculating totals.
examples.solution_text:
a. Scale the table value by the number of thousands borrowed.

$\begin{align*}\text{Monthly repayment}&=20.76\times\frac{28\,350}{1000}\\&=20.76\times28.35\\&=\$588.546\\&\approx\$588.55\end{align*}$

b. There are $5\times12=60$ monthly repayments. Use the rounded payment of $\$588.55$.

$\begin{align*}\text{Total repaid}&=588.55\times60\\&=\$35\,313.00\end{align*}$

c. Subtract the principal from the total repaid.

$\begin{align*}\text{Interest}&=\text{Total repaid}-\text{Principal}\\&=35\,313.00-28\,350\\&=\$6963.00\end{align*}$

methods.description: Convert years to months when needed, read the interest-rate row and term column, then multiply the repayment per $1000 by principal divided by 1000 and round to cents.
